sketchMechanisms: The `object` declaration creates a singleton — exactly one instance can ever exist, and it is created lazily the first time it is referenced.
A `weak` reference does not keep the referenced object alive; it automatically becomes `nil` when the object is deallocated, requiring optional unwrapping to access.
In Haskell, `fix` computes the fixed point of a function — a value defined entirely in terms of itself, enabling infinite self-reference that only resolves through laziness.
